content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks with `tsc --strict`, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 818 bytes min+gzip, with 100 bytes of my own code.

I couldn't compare results against the original lodash. `lodash` isn't installed in `node_modules`, and I was told not to install anything. Instead I ran the es-toolkit functions on sample inputs, and they gave the results I expect from lodash. The sample `kebabCase` inputs included `max44_id`, `HTMLParser`, `a1b` and `A.B-c d_E`. I didn't run the sample `keyBy` or `preview` inputs.

I also didn't measure the original's size or own-code bytes, so I can't say how the 100 bytes compares with the original.

- **`toSlug`:** uses `kebabCase` from `es-toolkit`. It gave `max44_id` → `max-44-id`, and `""` → `""`.
- **`byNameKey`:** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit`. Its key argument must be a function, so the adapter is `r => r.name` instead of the string `'name'`. Later rows overwrite earlier ones with the same name, as in lodash.
- **`preview`:** uses `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main `es-toolkit` package has no `truncate`, so this is the one call that comes from the compat build. It cuts at 24 characters and ends with `...`.

No lodash imports remain, and the exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged.
